Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

npmerger 0.0.0.9000

  • Part VII names are now matched on the canonical first name plus the surname. name_keys() parses each name with peopleparser, which strips titles and credentials and orders the name parts, and resolves nicknames and spelling variants (BOB → ROBERT, STEVEN → STEPHEN). leader_overlap(), merger_part7(), and so LEADER_P7, the leadership outcomes, and IN_BOTH all use it. merger_rules(name_key = "simple") restores the old first-and-last-token key (person_key()). Parsed names are cached for the session and saved in the project database (name_keys), so rebuilds do not parse them again. peopleparser (>= 0.2.0) is now an import. name_keys( workers = n ) passes workers to peopleparser::parse_names(); with 8 workers all 1.77 million Part VII names parse in about 4 minutes.

  • name_match_basis() (and md$name_matches) records why each person on both rosters matched: exact, a reviewed pair (nickname, spelling, cognate, compound), an unreviewed pair (misspelling, sound_alike), or indirect (linked only through the canonical form). REVIEW flags the last three. leadership_inspection() shows it as MATCH_BASIS.

  • The whole workflow now runs inside the package, into one project folder:

    • merger_project() creates a folder with the download cache, one DuckDB database, a logs/ folder, and a README. build_merger_database() runs the three stages ("merger", "match", "model") into it. Each stage writes its tables to the database, a log with package versions, git commit, settings, and sessionInfo(), and a row in build_log. load_merger_data(), load_match_data(), and load_model_data() rebuild each stage’s object from the database. db_tables(), db_read(), and db_write() give direct access. dev/build-project.R replaces dev/build-database.R and dev/build-matching.R.
    • merger_leadership() (CEO and board outcomes from the Part VII panel) and merger_typology() (deal structure, affiliation, relative size, and donor distress) were scripts; build_merger_data() now returns both as leadership and typology.
    • Models: build_model_data() assembles the treated units, control sets (including a match on the combined recipient + donor baseline), donor sums, and outcome panel once. merger_did() (long differences for every outcome and design), did_breakouts(), did_sensitivity() with did_variants(), did_event_study(), did_baseline_means(), did_funnel(), and did_composition() run from it. These replace the paper’s model script.
    • panel_measures() keeps the Part I revenue sources and Part IX functional and management expenses, so the models no longer re-read the e-file cache.
    • New vignette, “Workflow: from Schedule N to merger estimates”.

  • merger_fiscal_panel() no longer fails with current fiscal versions, whose compute_all_panel(append_to_df = FALSE) errors when re-sorting rows.

  • panel990 and fiscal are pinned to tested commits in Remotes. fixest and DBI are suggested.

  • Vignettes, the README, and examples use a narrower code style: one argument per line and each step’s result shown.

  • Outcome measures from the merger and financial-vulnerability literatures:

    • merger_measures() adds investment and other revenue, REVENUE_HHI (Part I revenue concentration, via revenue_hhi()), ADMIN_RATIO, revenue, expenses, and compensation per employee, and DEFICIT / NEG_NET_ASSETS flags. panel_measures() carries ADMIN_RATIO and REVENUE_HHI, and panel_columns() now reads Part I investment and other revenue.
    • trend_measures(): symmetric year-over-year growth (revenue, expenses, contributions, program revenue, net assets), trailing revenue coefficient of variation, and deficit-year counts. Windows never use future years or bridge filing gaps. merger_fiscal_panel(trends = TRUE) adds them by default.
    • tuckman_chang(): Tuckman-Chang (1991) vulnerability flags (bottom quintile on equity, margin, and admin costs, top quintile on revenue concentration), with cutoffs from a reference panel.
    • merger_proforma(): combined donor + recipient series that sums the organizations before the merger and uses the recipient alone after it, with ratios recomputed.

  • Classifier inspection tables: sn_labeled() stacks Schedule N Part I and Part II asset lines into one tidy table, with each part’s checkbox answers (sn_checkboxes()), the Part III text, the filing’s label and evidence, and IS_MERGER_RECIPIENT on lines to the merger recipient. sn_inspection() draws num non-overlapping samples stratified by label, with blank review columns. dev/build-inspection.R saves one 100-case table to data-dev/.

  • Matched comparison samples (vignette("matching")):

    • build_match_data() runs every matching step in one call and returns the sample, pool, candidates for each specification, balance, and coverage (match_coverage()).
    • get_panel() builds the full 990 / 990-EZ organization-year panel for every filer, with constant-dollar size, margin, equity ratio, months of cash, NTEE, and subsection (panel_measures(), real_dollars(), cpi_u(), ntee_level()).
    • merger_sample() keeps merger cases whose recipient filed in every year t-2..t+2, with t-3/t-2 baselines for donor and recipient.
    • match_pool() builds eligible comparison org-years: a full t-2..t+2 window around any year, and no Schedule N involvement nearby (schedule_n_events()).
    • match_candidates() finds every candidate in the same NTEE group within size and profitability (or fiscal-health) calipers, across any years, ranked by distance. match_balance() reports standardized differences.
    • dev/build-matching.R adds these tables to the database.
    • NTEE codes the current BMF lacks ("UNDEFINED", about a quarter of filers) are filled from the NCCS legacy BMF (legacy_ntee(), fill_ntee(), get_panel(ntee_legacy = TRUE)). NTEE_SOURCE records where each code came from.

  • Classifier rules revised after hand validation on 300 filings (dev/validation/; PLAN.md section 9). Agreement with hand labels rose from 62% to 70%, and merger recall from 51% to 71%.

    • merger_rules(min_top_share = 0.75): the default was 0.5. The share test now always applies, not only when there are several nonprofit recipients.
    • merger_rules(final_as_termination = TRUE): Part-II-only filings with the final-return box are treated as terminations. New TERMINATED column.
    • merger_rules(sn_text = TRUE): merger language in Schedule N’s own text (SN_MERGER_TEXT from sn_filings(), pattern sn_merger_pattern()) is merger evidence on its own, with BASIS = "sn_text".
    • merger_rules(promote = FALSE) is now the default. Only 1 of 13 promoted filings read as a merger. Set promote = TRUE for a broad definition.

  • build_merger_data() runs the whole pipeline and returns every table. It accepts pre-fetched inputs, so npmerger_example() runs offline.

  • Merger cases: build_merger_cases() (merger IDs, groups, and the merger year on each organization’s fiscal calendar), merger_roles(), transfer_value() (FMV by asset class, coverage of the donor’s assets, outlier flags), and asset_class().

  • Core data: get_core(), org_years() (one return per organization-year), and merger_measures() (harmonized 990 / 990-EZ revenue, expenses, assets, debt, staff costs, executive pay, grants, and overhead). get_bmf() adds NTEE codes and ruling years.

  • Analysis tables: merger_attributes() (donor and recipient attributes with five years of size history), merger_part7() (Part VII rosters from t-2 to t+2 with IN_BOTH), and merger_fiscal_panel() (measures, ‘fiscal’ ratios, an optional fixed-calibration index, and optional trailing smoothing via smooth_trailing()).

  • recover_recipient_ein() recovers missing recipient EINs by unique name and ZIP or state match against 990 filers (get_name_index()).

  • Merger evidence: get_evidence_tables() reads the 990 header, Part VII, Part VI, Schedule O, Schedule R, Schedule A, and mission tables for the donors and recipients in a set of filings. merger_features() adds: Part VII leadership overlap (leader_overlap()), counts of dissolving donors sharing a successor (add_donor_counts()), donor and recipient filing history and new-entity detection (add_filing_history()), corroborating disclosures (add_corroboration()), affiliation (add_affiliation()), and mission similarity (add_mission_similarity()).

  • classify_transactions() can promote an asset transfer to a merger when at least two corroborating signals agree, and records BASIS and N_CORROBORATE.

  • pkgdown site using the NODC pkgstyle template, and an overview vignette.

  • Initial package skeleton: Schedule N retrieval, flag/EIN/IRC-section parsers, transaction-level stacking of Schedule N Parts I and II, merger ID helpers, and default classification rules.

Developed by Jesse Lecy.
